'''''Aristolochia grandiflora''''', the '''pelican flower''', is a [[deciduous]] [[vine]] with one of the world's largest flowers that emits an odor that smells like rotting meat, attracting flies.
[[File:2023.12-532-242ap1 sideview of flower of Aristolochia grandiflora (ARIS) in the Singapore Botanic Gardens on sun17dec2023-1230h.jpg|thumb|right|Sideview of flower]]
[[Image:Aristolochia grandiflora detail.jpg|thumb|right|Detail of Pelican Flower with pollinators]]

==Description==
''Aristolochia grandiflora'' produces large solitary flowers from the axils of leaves. Leaves are [[Leaf shape|cordate]] and can be up to {{convert|25|cm|abbr=on}} wide.  Flowers are heart shaped: {{convert|10–30|cm|abbr=on}} wide and have tails that are up to {{convert|60|cm|abbr=on}}. The flower is green/white with purple/brown veins. The center of the flower is darker colored, which attracts pollinators along with a distinctive odor to its reproductive elements. The flower has three sections, utricle, tube and limb, characteristic to all Aristolochiaceae.<ref name= Trujillo >{{cite journal|last=Trujillo|first=C. G.|author2=A. N. Sersic|title=Floral biology of Aristolochia argentina (Aristolochiaceae)|journal=Flora|date=25 July 2005|volume=2001|pages=374–382}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
The plant is native to the [[Caribbean]] and [[Central America]], and has been introduced to [[Florida]] in the [[United States]] as an attractor of [[butterfly|butterflies]]. It is found in tropical forests near streams and gullies.

==Reproduction==
[[File:Aristolochia grandiflora MHNT.BOT.2025.29.1.jpg|thumb|''Aristolochia grandiflora'' ([[MHNT]])]]
''Aristolochia grandiflora'' is pollinated by breeding flies attracted by an odor produced by the flower. The odor is a combination of [[essential oils]]. Flies travel down the tubular part of the flower to the utricle where the [[plant reproduction|reproductive organs]] are found. The tube is lined with [[trichomes]] that direct the fly down to the utricle and prevent the fly from moving out. The reproduction contains three main phases. The first phase, the fly carrying pollen from other flowers pollinates the [[carpel]]. During the second phase, the [[stamen]] mature releasing pollen on the fly. This phase lasts one day. While trapped inside the flower, the fly eats nectar produced along the walls of the utricle. The trichomes then are signaled to wither, allowing for the fly to escape. The entire reproductive process lasts two days before flower [[senescence]] and [[abscission]] occur in the third phase.<ref name= Trujillo/>

==Uses==
''Aristolochia grandiflora'' has been used for ornamental purposes, as a food source, and in traditional medicine. ''A. grandiflora'' is a food source for [[swallowtail butterfly]] larvae. These butterflies become unpalatable to predators when they consume the [[terpene]]s in this plant.

==Chemical constituents==
The use of this plant poses a risk as it contains the toxin [[aristolochic acid]] which is [[carcinogenic]]. The [[USDA]] has banned all products containing this compound.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Heinrich|first=M|author2=Chan, J|author3= Wanke, S|author4= Neinhuis, C|author5= Simmonds, MS|title=Local uses of Aristolochia species and content of nephrotoxic aristolochic acid 1 and 2--a global assessment based on bibliographic sources.|journal=Journal of Ethnopharmacology|date=Aug 17, 2009|volume=125|issue=1|pages=108–44|pmid=19505558|doi=10.1016/j.jep.2009.05.028}}</ref> ''A. grandiflora'' contains many different [[alkaloid]]s (bisbenzylisoquinolinic and 8-benzylberberinic)<ref name= Holzbach >{{cite journal|last=Holzbach|first=Juliana C.|author2=Lopes, Lucia M. X.|title=Aristolactams and Alkamides of Aristolochia gigantea|journal=Molecules|date=21 December 2010|volume=15|issue=12|pages=9462–9472|doi=10.3390/molecules15129462|pmid=21178901|pmc=6259121|doi-access=free}}</ref> which aid in chemical defenses against insects and plant microbes.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Maiti|first=M.|author2=G. S. Kumar|title=Molecular aspects on the interaction of protoberberine, benzophenanthridine, and aristolochia group of alkaloids with nucleic acid structures and biological perspectives|journal=Medicinal Research Reviews|date=27 September 2007|volume=27|issue=5|pages=649–95|pmid=16894530|doi=10.1002/med.20087|s2cid=20805828}}</ref>  Chemicals in the essential oils include [[phellandrene|α-phellandrene]] and [[linalool]] from the stems and roots; [[germacrene D]] and [[elemene|γ-elemene]] from the leaves;  and [[Nerolidol|''trans''-nerolidol]] and [[geraniol]] from the stem and flower.<ref name= Holzbach/>

==Other species==
Other species of ''[[Aristolochia]]'' are also called "pelican flowers"; e.g. ''[[Aristolochia gigantea]]'' (giant pelican flower) and ''[[Aristolochia nana]]'' (tiny pelican flower).
